text: **The published checksum matches the bytes the user downloads.** Signing and checksumming are ORDERED and the order is silent when wrong: `codesign --force` **rewrites the binary in place**, whereas `notarytool submit` uploads a zip of a copy and we cannot staple a bare Mach-O, so notarisation leaves the file byte-identical. Therefore **sign BEFORE you checksum; notarise whenever.** Get it backwards and the formula ships a sha256 computed over pre-signature bytes -- which never fails for us and fails for **every single `brew install`**, at the point in the pipeline where we have the least visibility. Raised by dc 2026-08-15 from the Conflab port, where two sha256 lines are hand-maintained in the formula and a `release sync` command exists partly to heal this class of drift. **Hand-maintained checksums beside a generated artefact is the same shape as the hand-kept `SCHEMA_VERSION` beside the DDL in AC-02.7**, and it wants the same answer: the release path computes the checksum from the artefact it just signed, or a check refuses the publish. **MECHANISM BUILT 2026-08-15 (dc) as `int macos stage`, ahead of this row and independently of it**: it names artefacts per target triple from `rustc -vV` rather than `uname` (the artefact name is a claim about what the compiler targeted, and only the compiler can answer that), proves each **staged copy**, refuses outright unless every artefact is both signed and notarised, and only then checksums. **RESTRUCTURED at `3ab8844e` and this row is corrected to match (dc reported the drift; vc ruled): `stage` now COPIES ONLY and `checksum` proves-then-hashes, with `prepare` running stage/sign/notarize/checksum as one pass.** The staged copies are what get SIGNED, in a directory only `int macos` writes, so the de-notarisation race shrinks from the whole multi-minute sequence spanning a round trip to Apple down to one `ditto`. **And the refusal deliberately no longer deletes the staging directory** -- it removes only `SHA256SUMS.txt` and leaves both binaries in place. That was harmless when staging copied the build output; it is actively wrong now the staged files carry a signature and a notarisation, because discarding them spends another Apple round trip rebuilding something already correct. **The stale CLAIM cannot survive while the WORK does, which is the right split**: `formula` treats that file's existence as its proof, so removing it is sufficient to make the refusal binding. Canaried in both directions, which is the part that makes it evidence: a control that has only ever refused proves as little as one that has only ever passed. **The row stays unsatisfied because nothing is published yet** -- the mechanism existing is not the criterion; the published hash matching the published bytes is. **Two things to carry into the release path when the matrix is ruled:** the staged copies should be SIGNED rather than copied-after-signing, so the signed artefact lives where only the release pipeline writes (dc recorded the inversion and deliberately did not refactor proven code ahead of the ruling); and `verify_notarised` must stay ONE implementation serving both `verify` and `stage`, because a release-time check that is a second copy of the development-time one is a check that drifts. **STRENGTHENED 2026-08-17 (dc reported; vc ruled, and dc was right that the row always meant this): CONSISTENCY IS NOT CORRESPONDENCE.** Every check in this pipeline -- the round trip, the sums file, the classification refusal, the tag-exists check -- asks whether the bytes agree with EACH OTHER, and **a set of bytes built from a peer's uncommitted work is perfectly self-consistent.** Nothing asked whether these are the bytes the TAG names, so `publish` could establish that a tag exists and then publish artefacts with no evidence they came from it. **Two reachable routes, neither hypothetical**: `stage` COPIES out of `native/rust/target/release` rather than building, and that directory is shared mutable state in a clone four nodes write to (dc has twice measured a rebuild adopting a peer's in-flight edit); and the support tarball is archived with `tar -C "$ROOT"` from the WORKING TREE, so uncommitted shell ships verbatim -- and `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh` was dirty for most of 2026-08-17. **Fixed by recording the commit at `stage` and refusing at `publish`, compared against the TAG's commit rather than HEAD** (publishing may legitimately happen after the branch moves on; a HEAD comparison looks correct and would refuse every late publish, and there is a mutant for exactly that). **So the evidence line grows a second half rather than being replaced**: the checksum half proves the artefact is intact, and the commit half proves it is the RIGHT artefact, and neither implies the other

state.evidence: Signed before hashed, then checked from the user's side. int macos prepare proved each Mach-O, and the bundle inside Intent.app.zip, notarised from a quarantined copy BEFORE hashing. int macos publish re-downloaded all four v3.0.1 assets from the published URL, and every hash matches SHA256SUMS. The tap formula (fc32170) carries the same sha256 for intent (f1e6f38e), intentd (ab125a56) and support (2ca6bb1c). The cold tap install fetched and verified them (smoke --reinstall rc 0).
